objective: Use the user's inversion framework and scriptural/cross-cultural directions as a rule set for selecting real astronomical target regions and archive tests.
claim_boundary: The textual directions are treated as hypothesis-generation instructions, not as proof. A target becomes scientifically meaningful only when it produces a coordinate, observable, archival dataset, or falsifiable residual.

inversion_rules.textual_direction: Great governing light / nearest governing center
inversion_rules.inverted_physics_target: central mass anchor, supermassive black hole, intermediate-mass black hole, or compact dark object
inversion_rules.observable_translation: stellar orbits, astrometric accelerations, microlensing events, X-ray/radio flares, mass-profile residuals

inversion_rules.textual_direction: One day equals one thousand Earth years
inversion_rules.inverted_physics_target: period ladder or extreme gravitational time-dilation environment
inversion_rules.observable_translation: 1000-year Keplerian orbit radius around candidate mass; near-horizon clock condition; long-timescale lensing profile

inversion_rules.inverted_physics_target: Sirius system as a cross-cultural control field, not as proof
inversion_rules.observable_translation: Sirius A/B orbit, white-dwarf mass, Gaia/HST astrometry, unexplained residuals or additional-companion limits
microlensing without luminous lens, astrometric wobble, X-ray/radio quiet compact-object candidates

target_regions.name: Sagittarius A* control region
target_regions.why_selected: Best physical translation of an inverted governing-center instruction.
tests: Compare 1000-year Keplerian radius around Sgr A* to known S-star orbit scale.
Check whether any known orbit/time structure naturally matches the 1000-year reckoning.
Use Sgr A* as a control, not as a claimed identity.
target_regions.claim_status: high-value control target; no unique match yet

target_regions.name: Sirius A/B system
target_regions.why_selected: Best physical translation of the dog-star/hidden-dense-companion direction.
tests: Confirm Sirius B mass and orbit from modern data.
Search for residuals that would require an additional hidden mass.
Run a separate historical-source audit before treating Dogon material as evidence.
target_regions.claim_status: real astronomical control field; historical independence claim disputed

target_regions.name: Nearby hidden compact-object microlensing fields
target_regions.why_selected: Best direct analogue to the M31 method: infer invisible mass by light-curve distortion.
tests: Search for long-timescale events with no luminous lens counterpart.
Rank by achromaticity, baseline return, and astrometric residual.
Reject ordinary variables, blends, artifacts, and known stellar lenses first.
target_regions.claim_status: scientifically productive but not text-specific until a predicted region is defined

target_regions.name: M31-style extragalactic compact-object search extension
target_regions.why_selected: Uses the exact successful method family from PHAT-MICRO-0003: archival crowded-field transient/microlensing search.
tests: Extend candidate search for chromatic or hidden-lens anomalies.
Use PHAT-MICRO-0003 as method reference, not as proof of Kolob.
Build a compact-object anomaly population table.

execution_order: Build target manifest and constraint table.
Run source/coordinate verification against SIMBAD/VizieR when network access is available.
Run MAST metadata queries for Sirius and Sgr A*.
Build a compact-object archive search manifest for microlensing and Gaia residuals.
Only escalate to heavy data downloads after metadata shows usable products.
